signals.implication: Update constitutional clauses and compliance mappings for community operators.
signals.long_summary: There appears to be a unified narrative among effective altruism (EA) proponents suggesting that the common leftist perspective on artificial intelligence is that AI systems are merely "stochastic parrots," which implies that there is little cause for concern regarding their development and impact. The use of scare quotes indicates a critical stance towards this dismissal of potential AI risks. This discourse highlights a broader debate within the AI governance community about how AI is perceived and the implications of these views on policy and public understanding. Understanding these differing perspectives is crucial for our community as it affects how we approach the governance and development of AI technologies.

signals.title: Untitled
signals.summary: I think there are two key lessons from Linguistics as we deal with LLMs/chatbots being imposed on us everywhere. Grateful for Undark Magazine giving space for me to lay these out: https://undark.org/2026/09/25/interview-artificial-intelligence/
signals.implication: Track for context; no immediate governance action required.
signals.long_summary: Emily M. Bender discusses two essential lessons from linguistics relevant to the pervasive use of large language models (LLMs) and chatbots. She highlights the implications of these technologies on communication and understanding in our daily lives. Bender emphasizes the importance of critically examining how LLMs are integrated into society, suggesting that insights from linguistics can inform better approaches to their application and development. Engaging with her perspective is significant for those in the community aiming to understand AI's evolving role, as it encourages a deeper appreciation of the linguistic dimensions influencing technology's impact on society.
